short: ConvLSTM top layer (M06) is standard: new to ultrasound-to-speech, but a 2.1% MSE edge over BiLSTM, one speaker, one run; later work dropped it. No MCD or listener test (M12 behind).
position: The paper [@shandiz2022improved] changes one component (M06): a unidirectional ConvLSTM replaces the top layers of its group's 3D-CNN ultrasound front end, and test MSE on 80 standardized mel targets falls from 0.293 (3D-CNN) and 0.282 (3D-CNN + BiLSTM) to 0.276, 5.8% and 2.1% relative (inference). M06 is standard: the layer is new to ultrasound-to-speech mapping (9 ConvLSTM pattern matches among 148 ultrasound studies, none an earlier speech-output study; Appendix), but the edge over the BiLSTM is one run on one speaker, with dropout raised from 0.3 to 0.35 and pooling changed alongside (Table 1). Later work dropped it [@toth2023adaptation; @sonkar2026tongue2speech]. Evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work, not the field's typical practice: MSE and mean R² only, although the group's listener-tested studies of this speaker and of the same WaveGlow synthesis stage [@csapo2017dnn; @grosz2018f0; @csapo2020waveglow] predate it. "Smaller and faster" (Abstract) is unmeasured.
